content:
CarPlay can make any vehicle feel more comfortable and familiar, but the original experience may not be perfect.

Some car models still require a wired connection, and some models do not support CarPlay at all, let alone charging and cooling the iPhone during long drives.

The good news is that improving these issues does not require a large investment. The affordable accessories introduced below cover wireless CarPlay, MagSafe charging, cable management, and even adding displays to older vehicles.

Convert wired CarPlay to wireless

If your vehicle already supports wired CarPlay, the Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 lets you cut the cord while retaining the factory touchscreen, steering wheel control buttons, built-in microphone, and original audio system.

This compact adapter features USB-A and USB-C ports. After the initial pairing, it automatically reconnects every time the vehicle is started. It also supports wireless Android Auto for devices running Android 11 and above, making it ideal for vehicles shared between iPhone and Android users.

One thing to note: this adapter must be used with factory-installed wired CarPlay and cannot add CarPlay functionality to vehicles that do not support it.

The Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 is priced at $43.99, with free shipping for Prime members.

Add CarPlay to almost any older vehicle

For vehicles without CarPlay, an external display is usually the simplest upgrade option. The Krunia 9.26-inch portable CarPlay display, priced at $89.99, adds wireless CarPlay without removing the factory head unit.

The display supports Bluetooth, AUX, and FM audio connections, and is compatible with Siri, Android Auto, and OTA firmware updates. The accessory kit also includes a reversing camera, but installation requires routing a cable to the rear of the vehicle.

This is an attractive compromise for owners who want CarPlay but do not want to replace the factory infotainment system.

Install a permanent CarPlay head unit

A portable display may not suit every dashboard layout. For a cleaner, more permanent installation, the BOSS Audio BVCP9700A is a relatively affordable double-DIN head unit featuring a 7-inch touchscreen, with support for Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, and a reversing camera.

This head unit is priced at $164.99, but buyers should confirm vehicle compatibility before ordering. Installation kits, wiring harnesses, steering wheel control adapters, or professional installation services may add to the overall cost.

Keep your iPhone cool while charging

Wireless charging, navigation, sunlight, and a hot dashboard all combined create a tough test for any iPhone. The ESR CryoBoost MagSafe car charger has a built-in cooling fan and pairs with a magnetic air vent or dashboard mount, providing wireless charging with active cooling. Priced at $29.99, it is especially suited for drivers using wireless CarPlay who still want to charge their iPhone on long journeys.

Want a cleaner setup? Skip charging with a MagSafe mount

Not every journey requires wireless charging. The standard ESR MagSafe car mount holds your iPhone on the dashboard or air vent, with no extra charging cable needed.

Priced at $15.99, it comes with a metal magnetic ring for iPhones or cases without built-in magnets. In hot climates, skipping charging—which generates additional heat—may actually be the better choice.

Replace an unreliable CarPlay cable

Many CarPlay issues stem from aging or poorly connected cables. The Anker Nano USB-A to USB-C CarPlay cable features a braided design and is built for data transfer on newer USB-C iPhones, priced at $11.99.

Drivers using an iPhone 14 or older can opt for the Anker PowerLine Flow USB-A to Lightning cable, priced at $17.99.

Add fast charging to improve the experience

The USB port that supports wired CarPlay often charges slowly. The Anker 323 car charger plugs into the 12V power socket and provides one USB-C port and one USB-A port.

Priced at just $14.99, it can charge passengers' phones and power other accessories without interfering with the vehicle's CarPlay connection; when paired with wireless CarPlay, it also speeds up charging.

Tidy up your installation and cabling

A set of adhesive cable clips, priced at $6.99, can make the installation of a portable CarPlay display or a wired phone mount look much neater. These clips route cables along the edges of the dashboard, keeping them away from the gear stick, pedals, or cup holders.

You don't need to buy a new car or upgrade your audio system significantly to enjoy CarPlay. Depending on your vehicle's existing features, spending anywhere from $12 on a better cable to around $90 on a complete portable display can greatly enhance the daily experience.

Want to get even more out of CarPlay? Check out 9to5Mac's curated list of over 120 iPhone apps that support CarPlay.
